$comment: This registry's copy of the default registry's tbb 2023.1.0 (microsoft/vcpkg afa249f1, git-tree afe9558e, the two upstream files verbatim) with two changes, carried over from this port's 2022.1.0#1 (M4 of carbon-mobile-exp-v8-upgrade, 2026-11-17: oneTBB 2023.1.0 still needs both). (1) The hwloc default feature keeps upstream's platform guard `!static & !osx & !uwp` and gains `& !android`: it lies dormant wherever tbb is static and wakes up wherever a triplet makes tbb shared, which arm64-android-release.cmake does (for the file-scope tbb::global_control in trinity/TriDevice.cpp); hwloc then joins the Android closure and fails to link its lstopo utility (undefined setJNIEnv / output_android -- its Android build expects the hwloc JNI app around it). A top-level `default-features: false` on trinity's own tbb dependency cannot switch it off, because openvdb and carbon-audio also depend on tbb and their edges still request the defaults. Windows and iOS, where tbb is shared too, keep TBBBind exactly as upstream. (2) Android only: android-lld-undefined-version.patch appends -Wl,--undefined-version to TBB_LIB_LINK_FLAGS, because the lin64 .def version scripts keep a local: list of names that no longer exist (ITT_DoOneTimeInitialization, __intel_*; still there in 2023.1.0) and the NDK r27 lld defaults to --no-undefined-version plus --fatal-warnings, which fails libtbbmalloc.so's link. The patch was regenerated against 2023.1.0's cmake/compilers/Clang.cmake (its relro line now also carries -z,noexecstack); 2022.1.0's fix-lang and fix-gcc-without-gas patches are upstream in 2023.1.0 and went. It shadows the default registry's tbb because a consumer lists `tbb` under this registry's packages (trinity does); port-version 1 is there so the package's version string, and its ABI hash, differ from the default registry's 2023.1.0#0. Drop `tbb` from the consumers' packages lists, and this port, when the default-registry baseline moves past a tbb whose .def files and Android hwloc build are fixed.
name: tbb

hwloc.description: Builds TBB with TBBBind support for Hybrid CPUs or NUMA architectures.
